title: Unify credential decorator and telemetry for generator-stream ergonomics across SDKs (py/ts/go)
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Introduce credential decorator helper and lightweight telemetry hooks for generator/pull-stream APIs across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Backwards-compatible, opt-in ergonomics and minor version bumps for each SDK.
description:
Motivation: cross-SDK users reported duplicated setup for credential refresh, inconsistent telemetry around generator/pull-stream consumption, and friction when wiring retry timing into stream lifecycles. This PR introduces a small, opinionated credential decorator (CredDecorator) and lightweight stream telemetry hooks (stream.start/stream.chunk/stream.finish) implemented in Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Goals: 1) Reduce boilerplate for token refresh and retry hints in user code, 2) Surface consistent per-stream telemetry events to help product and infra correlate observed client-side retries with server-side cost/latency, 3) Keep the change opt-in and non-breaking.

Summary of changes (by SDK):
- Python SDK (redwood-sdk-python): add redwood.auth.CredDecorator, a contextmanager-friendly decorator that wraps call/session factories and exposes on_refresh and on_error callbacks; add stream telemetry hooks to generator StreamIterator; bump SDK minor to 1.12.0. Tests added for edge refresh races and heartbeat jitter.
- TypeScript SDK (redwood-sdk-typescript): add CredDecorator class + utility types; add StreamTelemetry interface and optional hooks on async iterators; expose a small convenience wrapper createDecoratedClient(); bump SDK minor to 1.28.1. Includes typed examples in docs.
- Go SDK (redwood-sdk-go): introduce cred.Decorator interface and DecorateClient helper; add telemetry callbacks on the PullStream type (Start/Chunk/Finish); bump SDK minor to v1.8.3. Add integration test exercising decorator + backoff presets.

Testing & CI: initial run surfaced two flaky generator tests under older node versions; adjusted test matrix to skip node12 in the new generator-focused matrix and added targeted unit tests that deterministically mock clock. Final CI status: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration on linux/amd64, go vet, typecheck). A follow-up job ran downstream SDK consumers smoke-tests and passed.

Review conversation (selected highlights):
- Liam Hart: "Nice reduction in boilerplate. Can we make the Python decorator play nicely with existing retry decorators?" Author: "CredDecorator composes with existing retry decorators; updated README showing composition and added a regression test." 
- Daniela Ruiz: "Telemetry events look good, but please make sure we don't leak sensitive headers in events." Author: "Telemetry only exposes metadata: stream_id, lifecycle_phase, duration_ms, error_code; removed header capture in telemetry shim." 
- Mats: "Prefer explicit opt-in in TS example rather than global enablement." Author: "Switched examples to explicit createDecoratedClient() pattern; SDK defaults remain unchanged."

Migration notes: the default behavior is unchanged. To opt into the ergonomics, users call the new decorator factory (examples in SDK docs). No API surface that existed before was removed. There is a small behavior change for users who had hand-rolled telemetry: they may see additional standardized events if they enable decorator telemetry. The PR adds examples and a short migration section in each SDK CHANGELOG.

Rollout plan: merged to main, published staged minor releases to internal package registries, and coordinated with integrations team to bump pinned versions in the internal examples repo next week. Will monitor client telemetry for 72h to ensure no increase in error surface (alert created: ENG-2102-stream-telemetry-regression).

Notes: this PR intentionally kept the decorator responsibilities small (token lifecycle and light telemetry) and left richer orchestration (prefetch pools, lease managers) to follow-up tasks. Related items: ENG-2102 (stream telemetry), ENG-2120 (sdk ergonomics follow-up).
notes: Author ran manual smoke on a sample app (py/ts/go) and validated metrics in staging. No infra changes required.
